payload.title: Staging for Pretext sites: drafts content source, Cognito/editor gate, SITE_ENV guards
payload.description:
## Goal
Staging for Pretext (SSR) sites: a `staging` deployment of the same app that shows DRAFT items as if published, only to signed-in `editor`/`admin` users of the site's own Cognito, with enforcement in AppSync (not just the page). Includes the shared `SITE_ENV` guard helper (noindex, `Disallow: /`, banner, no analytics) used by Pretext and by the static staging route (`PPY-f00c89`). Implements spike findings 7 (SSR must use identityPool for published and userPool only for drafts) and the unexercised guards of finding (f).

## Context (verified)
- `lib/graphql-content-repository.ts` implements `ContentRepository` (`lib/content-types.ts` L81-90) over the PUBLISHED models: `AUTH_MODE = "identityPool"` (L20) is used in ~10 call sites; four accessors pick the models: `getPublishedEditionModel` (L513), `getPublishedEditionItemModel` (L519), `getPublishedItemModel` (L525), `getPublishedMediaAssetModel` (L531); `withReaderGraphQLContext` (L133-146) wraps every public method in `runWithAmplifyServerContext({ nextServerContext: null, ... })` from `lib/amplify-server-runtime.ts` (`getAmplifyServerRuntime()`, `Amplify.configure(config, { ssr: true })`, guest access enabled); `listItemsByTypeStatus` uses `typeStatus` `"article#published"` (L23).
- `lib/cached-content-repository.ts` wraps the repository in `unstable_cache` (`READER_REVALIDATE_SECONDS = 3600`, `lib/reader-route-config.ts`); `lib/content-repository.ts` `contentRepository` delegates to `graphqlContentRepository`.
- `PAPYRUS_CONTENT_SOURCE` is set in the infra build specs (`infra/amplify-app-shell/lib/amplify-app-shell.ts` L100, `amplify.yml` L14) but NOT read by any code today.
- Auth rules: `Item`, `Edition`, `EditionItem`, `MediaAsset` allow only groups `editor`/`admin` (+ custom JWT lane): `amplify/data/schema.ts` Item block ends `allow.groups(contentWriteGroups), allow.custom()...`; `Published*` allow `guest` read + groups. Spike result: a signed-in non-editor cannot read `PublishedItem` over userPool; guest/identityPool works; signed-in editor reads `Item` over userPool.
- Client auth: `components/amplify-client-provider.tsx` configures Amplify with `{ ssr: true }` and cookie token storage (`CookieStorage`), so the Next server can read the session from request cookies. `/newsroom` shows the sign-in UI when `shell.phase` is `signedOut`/`forbidden` (`components/topic-steering-workspace.tsx` ~L15424-15454; `lib/news-desk-session.ts`).
- `middleware.ts` (after `PPY-672ea6`): only newsroom-root-path rewriting. There is no `robots`/`SITE_ENV` handling in Papyrus (the pattern to copy is `Anth.us-Papyrus` `web/site_env.py` on `origin/main`: guarded unless `SITE_ENV=production` AND branch `main`).
- Decision recorded: drafts mode reads the `Item` rows through the SAME normalizers as `PublishedItem` (`normalizeArticle`, `normalizePublicationItem`): the columns they read (`slug, section, headline, title, deck, byline, dateline, publishedAt, bodyIr, bodyMarkus, metadata, editorial, pullQuotes`, `MediaAsset` rows) exist on both models, so no separate TypeScript "projectItemToPublished" is needed (YAGNI); the Python projection (`PPY-b3a10e`) stays the single writer of `Published*`.
- Unsolved by design: Pretext index pages list items through EDITIONS (`loadEditionContent` -> `Edition`/`EditionItem`). CMS-authored articles that are not in an edition are reachable at `/articles/<slug>` (and `listArticleSlugs()`), not on edition pages. Drafts mode mirrors that: it reads `Edition`/`EditionItem` (any status) so edition planning previews work; standalone drafts show at `/articles/<slug>`.

## Exact changes
1. `lib/site-env.ts` (new): `export type SiteEnv = "production" | "staging" | "development"`; `getSiteEnv()` from `SITE_ENV` (default `development`; `production` only when `SITE_ENV=production` and (`AWS_BRANCH` is unset or `main`) else `staging`/`development` as given; any other value throws); `isIndexable()`, `showStagingBanner()`, `analyticsAllowed()` (production only); `assertContentSourceMatchesEnv()`: `PAPYRUS_CONTENT_SOURCE=drafts` requires `SITE_ENV=staging`, and `SITE_ENV=staging` with source `published` is allowed (static staging), but `drafts` anywhere else throws at startup. Call it from `lib/content-repository.ts` module scope.
2. Guards: `app/robots.ts` (new route file): production -> `{ rules: { userAgent: "*", allow: "/" } }`, otherwise `{ rules: { userAgent: "*", disallow: "/" } }`; `app/layout.tsx` `generateMetadata`: add `robots: { index: false, follow: false }` unless `isIndexable()`; `components/staging-banner.tsx` (new, server component, text "STAGING: drafts shown as published", `data-staging-banner`) rendered in `app/layout.tsx` body when `showStagingBanner()`; `middleware.ts`: when not indexable add `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow` to every response. Grep for analytics scripts (`rg -n "gtag|googletagmanager|plausible|analytics" app components lib`) and wrap whatever exists with `analyticsAllowed()` (if none exists, only the helper is added).
3. Source switch without refactoring the file into closures: `lib/content-source-context.ts` (new): `AsyncLocalStorage<{ source: "published" | "drafts"; cookies?: () => ... }>`; in `lib/graphql-content-repository.ts` replace the module constant `AUTH_MODE` by `authMode()` (`"userPool"` in drafts, else `"identityPool"`), and make the four model accessors return `Edition`/`EditionItem`/`Item`/`MediaAsset` models in drafts mode (their query names differ: `editionBySlug`, `listEditionsByStatusAndPublishedAt`, `listEditionItemsByEditionAndSortKey({ editionId })`, `itemBySlug`, `listItemsByTypeStatusAndPublishedAt`, `listMediaAssetsByItemAndSortKey({ itemId })`: add a small adapter object per source with the same method names the file already calls). In drafts mode `withReaderGraphQLContext` runs `runWithAmplifyServerContext({ nextServerContext: { cookies } , ... })` with `cookies` from `next/headers`, and `listItemsByTypeStatus` lists both `"<type>#draft"` and `"<type>#published"`; status checks (`item.status !== "published"` in `getArticle`, `listArticleSlugs`) accept `draft` in drafts mode. Export `normalizeArticle`/`normalizePublicationItem` only if needed by tests.
4. Cache: `lib/cached-content-repository.ts` `withReaderCache`: when `process.env.PAPYRUS_CONTENT_SOURCE === "drafts"` return `loader()` uncached (never cache user-scoped draft reads; also avoids staging serving 1-hour-old drafts).
5. Gate: `lib/staging-gate.ts` (new): `async function getStagingAccess(request): Promise<"anonymous" | "forbidden" | "ok">` using `runWithAmplifyServerContext({ nextServerContext: { request, response } })` + `fetchAuthSession` from `aws-amplify/auth/server`; groups from `tokens.idToken.payload["cognito:groups"]` (must include `editor` or `admin`). `middleware.ts`: when `getSiteEnv() === "staging"` and the path is not `/_next`, `/api`, favicon, icon, or `/newsroom*`: `anonymous` -> redirect to `/newsroom` (the sign-in lives there on the same origin; the staging origin must be in `PAPYRUS_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URLS`, `PPY-39f928`), `forbidden` -> `new NextResponse("Staging is limited to editors and admins.", { status: 403 })`. The page gate is a convenience; AppSync is the enforcement (a non-editor gets `Unauthorized` on `Item`).
6. `scripts/check-staging-guards.mjs <base-url> <staging|production>` (new): fetches `/robots.txt` and `/` and asserts: staging -> `Disallow: /`, `<meta name="robots" content="noindex`, `data-staging-banner`, and (unauthenticated) a 307 to `/newsroom`; production -> `Allow: /`, no noindex, no banner. Used in acceptance and CI.
7. Docs: `docs/site-hosting.md` section on `PAPYRUS_CONTENT_SOURCE`/`SITE_ENV` (production never sets `drafts`).

## Data shapes
Env per deployment: production `SITE_ENV=production` (`PAPYRUS_CONTENT_SOURCE` unset or `published`); staging `SITE_ENV=staging PAPYRUS_CONTENT_SOURCE=drafts` (Pretext) or `SITE_ENV=staging PAPYRUS_CONTENT_SOURCE=published` + `PAPYRUS_STAGING_PREVIEW=static` (`PPY-f00c89`). `getStagingAccess` returns one of three strings; the 403 body is plain text.

## Tests
- TS unit `scripts/test-site-env.ts` (tsx): matrix of `SITE_ENV`/`AWS_BRANCH` values; `assertContentSourceMatchesEnv` throws for `drafts` + `production`; `scripts/test-content-source.ts`: with a mocked Amplify data client, drafts mode calls `Item.itemBySlug` with `authMode: "userPool"` and published mode calls `PublishedItem.publishedItemBySlug` with `identityPool`; uncached in drafts mode.
- Schema-subset test `scripts/test-content-column-parity.ts`: every key of `GraphQLItem` (the type in `graphql-content-repository.ts`) exists in both the `Item` and `PublishedItem` blocks of `amplify/data/schema.ts` (regex), guarding the "same normalizers" decision.
- Gherkin (cucumber): `features/staging-guards.feature`: "A staging deployment is not indexable and says so" (runs against `SITE_ENV=staging npm run dev`; uses `scripts/check-staging-guards.mjs` semantics through steps), "A production deployment is indexable". Tag `@staging`; in `cucumber.js` keep default tags excluding `@staging` unless env `SITE_ENV=staging`.
- Auth proof (sandbox, same pattern as spike `scripts/spike-auth-test.mjs`; test users created and deleted in the script, random in-memory password, nothing printed): editor reads a draft via the staging route and sees the banner; anonymous is redirected; a signed-in user in neither group gets the 403 page AND `Item` read over userPool returns `Unauthorized`; guest cannot read the draft slug (404). Commit the script as `scripts/staging-auth-test.mjs`; run it in the PR and paste the 12-check output.

## Acceptance checks
- `npx tsx scripts/test-site-env.ts && npx tsx scripts/test-content-source.ts && npx tsx scripts/test-content-column-parity.ts` pass; `npx tsc --noEmit`.
- `SITE_ENV=staging PAPYRUS_CONTENT_SOURCE=drafts npm run dev` + `node scripts/check-staging-guards.mjs http://localhost:3001 staging` exits 0; with `SITE_ENV=production` and `check-staging-guards.mjs ... production` exits 0; `SITE_ENV=production PAPYRUS_CONTENT_SOURCE=drafts npm run dev` refuses to start with the guard message.
- Sandbox: `node scripts/staging-auth-test.mjs` passes all checks.

## Dependencies
Blocked by `PPY-cddfb8` (same file `graphql-content-repository.ts`; PRT changes body handling first), `PPY-672ea6` (middleware, layout), `PPY-44a0f9`/`PPY-b3a10e` only for realistic test data (drafts have `bodyIr`). Blocks `PPY-f00c89` (shares `lib/site-env.ts`, `lib/staging-gate.ts`, middleware), `PPY-8ef4ca` (preview link) softly, `PPY-39f928` verification of staging branch config.

## Risks
- Server-side session in middleware: Amplify's `runWithAmplifyServerContext` works in Next middleware (documented pattern) but token refresh writes cookies on the response; implement per Amplify docs and test token expiry once.
- Drafts mode hits userPool-protected models on every request (no cache): fine for an editor-only site; do not enable on production.
- Edition-based index pages (see Context) are the known gap for CMS-authored items; flagged for Phase 4.
- Hosted-UI sign-in on the staging origin needs the origin in the Cognito callback list (`PAPYRUS_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URLS`, changed in `PPY-39f928`; email/password sign-in works without it).

## Needs Ryan
Nothing for the code. Staging reads the production backend (decision), so the first real staging check belongs to the Pilobol.us migration (Phase 3).

## Common rules (apply to every Phase 2 ticket)
- Work from a clean worktree of `origin/develop` (`git -C /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus fetch origin && git worktree add ../Papyrus-worktrees/<this-ticket> -b feature/PPY-3e5e9d-<slug> origin/develop`). Never commit to `develop` or `main`; open a PR into `develop`; never merge to `main`. Conventional-commit messages. Update this ticket with branch, PR link and the verification output.
- `AGENTS.md` rules that bind this work: no backward-compatibility shims or fallbacks (clean breaks); backend tooling in Python unless noted; Pretext owns text measurement (do not measure DOM in React); read `AGENTS.local.md` before ANY AWS/Amplify/sandbox command; never run `ampx pipeline-deploy` locally (sandbox only).
- Note on language direction: Ryan's 2026-10-05 correction (epic comment 4174c5) says Papyrus is being ported from Python to TypeScript. Phase 2 follows the approved design in docs/standard-site.md (Python CLI/Lambdas + `papyrus-newsroom`). Keep new Python logic in small pure functions with fixture-driven tests so it can be ported; do not add new Python dependencies beyond those named here.
- Tests: Python unit tests are `unittest` under `procedures/newsroom/tests/` (run: `poetry run python -m unittest procedures.newsroom.tests.<module> -v`); backend Gherkin is `behave` under `features_backend/` with steps in `features_backend/steps/` (run: `poetry run behave features_backend/<file>.feature`); UI Gherkin is cucumber-js + Playwright under `features/` (run against a dev server: `npm run dev` then `PAPYRUS_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3001 npx cucumber-js features/<file>.feature`); TypeScript unit tests are `scripts/test-*.ts` run with `npx tsx` (add an npm script `test:<name>` in package.json).
- Install: `poetry install --extras "newsroom markus"` and `npm ci`. Verify `markus --version` prints 0.5.1 (PyPI `anthus-markus` 0.5.1 emits IR `schema_version: 1`).
